case_scope: GCC public wealth and migrant claimant-perimeter stress screen

jurisdictional_mobility_gate.note: The case remains a fail because migrant workers can be inside the productive economy but outside durable public-wealth, social-protection, family-unity, and appeal perimeters.

migrant_claimant_perimeter_exclusion.note: Migrant-worker shares and de jure/de facto social-protection gaps make claimant-perimeter exclusion a direct wealth problem, not merely immigration administration.

portable_social_rights_for_migrants.note: Portability must be proved for pensions, injury, end-of-service benefits, health coverage, unemployment/job loss, and family survivors across origin and destination.

remittance_or_transnational_support_burd.note: Remittances can support origin households, but they can also replace public floors and transfer care/debt risk across borders.

appeal_and_error_correction_access.note: Legal access is not enough if sponsor control, deportability, language, cost, or job loss prevents timely appeal and remedy conversion.

proof_debt: country-specific migrant worker share and sectors
wage, injury, and end-of-service claim outcomes

gate_13_jurisdictional_mobility.why: Gate 13 is blocked: a wealth system cannot pass if migrant workers produce public/private wealth while remaining outside durable claimant perimeters and remedy rails.

gate_11_enforceability.why: Remedies need sponsor-independent access, language/cost support, no retaliation/deportability penalty, and portable collection.

evidence_debt_register.question: country-specific migrant worker share and sectors
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Use ILO and national statistics to map migrant shares by sector, nationality, gender, domestic work, construction, and service occupations.

evidence_debt_register.question: social-protection access by migrant category
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Compare de jure and de facto access to pensions, health care, injury compensation, unemployment/job-loss protection, and family benefits.

evidence_debt_register.question: sponsorship/job-loss/deportability interaction
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Measure whether job loss, sponsor control, recruitment debt, or visa cancellation blocks remedy access before claims mature.

evidence_debt_register.question: wage, injury, and end-of-service claim outcomes
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Collect complaint, settlement, court, labor-ministry, insurance, and end-of-service payout evidence, including time-to-payment.

evidence_debt_register.question: portability to origin countries
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Track whether accrued benefits, savings, claims, and health/injury protections follow workers and survivors across borders.

evidence_debt_register.question: family-unity and survivor-claim treatment
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Score whether migrant households can preserve family integrity, survivor benefits, and remittance continuity after death, injury, deportation, or job loss.

policy_pathway: Score GCC public wealth and remittance cases through migrant claimant perimeter, not national aggregate wealth alone.
Require social-protection portability, sponsor-independent remedy access, wage/injury/end-of-service collection, and family/survivor continuity before any improved calibration.
validation_notes: rev0336 removed stale jurisdictional_mobility_gate_seed calibration label only after current-law, source-fit, currentness, and evidence-debt hardening.
